title: What is an emergency?
text: An emergency is a sudden, dangerous moment that needs help fast. Someone gets hurt, a fire starts, or the ground shakes.

title: Hazards and disasters
text: A hazard is something that can hurt us, like a typhoon, flood, earthquake, fire or volcano. It becomes a disaster when it harms many people and places.

title: Why the Philippines?
text: Our country sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanoes happen. About 20 typhoons also visit us every year.

title: Know, Plan, Pack
text: KNOW the hazards where you live. PLAN with your family where to meet. PACK a Go Bag with water, food, a flashlight and a whistle.

title: Listen for warnings
text: PAGASA warns us about typhoons and heavy rain. PHIVOLCS watches earthquakes and volcanoes. Listen to the radio, sirens, and your school bell.

title: Stay calm, find an adult
text: When something scary happens, take a deep breath. Tell a trusted adult right away, like your teacher, parent, or a barangay official.

title: Call 911 for help
text: 911 is the emergency hotline in the Philippines. Say what happened and where you are. Stay on the phone until they tell you to hang up.

title: The ground can shake!
text: An earthquake happens when big rocks deep under the ground suddenly move. The Philippines has many earthquakes, so every explorer should be ready.

title: Get ready before it happens
text: Know the safe spots in your home and school. Keep heavy things on low shelves. Pack a Go Bag with water, a flashlight and a whistle.

title: DUCK!
text: When the shaking starts, drop down to your hands and knees right away. This keeps you from falling over.

title: COVER!
text: Crawl under a strong table or desk. Protect your head and neck with your arms.

title: HOLD!
text: Hold on to a leg of the table. If the table moves, move with it. Stay there until the shaking stops.

title: Stay away from danger
text: Keep away from windows, glass, shelves and hanging things. They can break or fall.

title: After the shaking
text: Wait for your teacher. Walk calmly to the open area in a line. Do not push, run, or go back inside. Small shakes called aftershocks may come.

title: Fire can help or hurt
text: Fire helps us cook, but uncontrolled fire can spread quickly. Fire safety means preventing fires, preparing an escape plan, and leaving safely.

title: Be a fire safety detective
text: Candles near paper or curtains, damaged wires, and overloaded outlets can start fires. Stay away and tell a trusted adult. Never play with matches or lighters.

title: What keeps a fire burning?
text: Fire needs heat, fuel, and oxygen. Paper and wood are fuels. Air supplies oxygen. Together these make the fire triangle.

title: Plan your way out
text: Learn your main exit and another way out in case it is blocked. Keep exits clear. Choose an outside meeting place with your family or class, and practice your plan.

title: Hear the alarm? Leave safely
text: Stop your activity and follow your teacher along the safe escape route. Leave bags behind. Walk without pushing. Use stairs, not elevators.

title: Stay low and go
text: Smoke makes it hard to see and breathe. Stay low as you move toward a safe exit. Do not hide or go toward the fire. Use another safe route if your way is blocked.

title: Stop, Drop, and Roll
text: If your CLOTHES catch fire, STOP moving. DROP to the ground and cover your face with your hands. ROLL over the flames until they go out. Then get adult help.

title: Get out and stay out
text: Go to the outside assembly area. Stay with your class so your teacher can count everyone. Never go back for a bag, phone, or pet. Tell an adult if someone is missing.

title: Let trained helpers handle fire
text: From a safe place, alert an adult and call emergency responders. Explain what happened and where. Extinguishers are for trained people with the right equipment and a safe escape route.

title: Water rises fast!
text: Heavy rain can cause floodwaters to rise quickly. Never play in floodwaters—they can be deep, dirty, and carry dangerous currents.

title: Move to high ground
text: If floodwaters start coming into your home or neighborhood, move to a higher floor or elevated safe area immediately.

title: Strong winds and heavy rain
text: Typhoons bring heavy rain and strong winds that can blow away roofs or tear down trees. Stay inside a safe house!

title: Prepare before the storm hits
text: Charge emergency lights, charge phones, lock doors and windows, and bring pets inside before wind gets strong.

title: Why we practice drills
text: Drills practice our brain and feet so we know exactly what to do when real alarms sound. Stay calm and listen to your teacher.

title: Walk in an orderly line
text: Follow the designated exit route to the open evacuation area. Protect your head with your arms or bag if needed.

title: What is a Go Bag?
text: A Go Bag is a ready backpack filled with essential supplies you can grab immediately when an emergency evacuation happens.

title: Essential Go Bag items
text: Pack clean water, non-perishable food, flashlight, whistle, emergency money, first-aid kit, and family emergency contact cards.

title: Call 911 in real danger
text: In the Philippines, 911 is the national emergency number. Call when someone is hurt, there is a fire, or a crime is happening.

title: What to say to the responder
text: Stay calm. Tell them: 1. Where you are. 2. What happened. 3. Who needs help. Listen carefully to instructions.

title: Safe distance from strangers
text: A stranger is anyone you and your parents do not know well. Always keep a safe distance and never accept rides or gifts without permission.

title: No, Go, Tell!
text: If someone makes you feel unsafe: Say NO loudly, GO away fast to a crowded safe spot, and TELL a trusted adult right away.

title: Keep personal details private
text: Never share your full name, home address, school, or passwords online. Protect your digital footprint!

title: Be kind online & report mean words
text: Cyberbullying means using words or pictures to hurt others online. Be respectful online. If someone is mean, don’t reply—tell a parent or teacher.

title: Cross at pedestrian lanes
text: Always use pedestrian crosswalks or footbridges. Stop, look left, look right, and look left again before stepping off the curb.

title: Traffic light colors
text: RED means STOP. YELLOW means SLOW DOWN / CAUTION. GREEN means GO (if crosswalk is clear). Always wait for pedestrian light signal!
